text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
American President of the Confederate States, JEFFERSON DAVIS, was born in 1808.
English traveller in early Australia PHILIP LORIMER (known as 'OLD PHIL THE POET') was born in 1843. He once wrote "Queensland - Thou art a land of pest. From flies and fleas we ne'er can rest".
Australian politician WILLIAM ARCHIBALD was born in 1850.
American actress PAULETTE GODDARD, who starred in CHARLIE CHAPLIN's "Modern Times" and "The Great Dictator" (and secretly married the famous comedian on the 1st of June 1933), was born in 1911.
Australian swimming coach FORBES CARLILE was born in 1921.
American actor TONY CURTIS (born BERNARD SCHWARTZ), whose many films included "Some Like It Hot" (with JACK LEMMON and MARILYN MONROE in 1959) and "The Boston Strangler" (1968), was born in 1925.
American poet ALLAN GINSBERG was born in 1926.
British guitarist MICKEY FINN, who joined "T-Rex" in 1969, was born in 1947.

American singer SUZI QUATRO, who found hits with "Can The Can" (1973), "48 Crash" (1973) and "Devil Gate Drive" (1974), was born in 1950. The only song to become a hit in the United States was the duet with CHRIS NORMAN (lead singer from the group "Smokie"), "Stumblin' In" in 1978/79.
Canadian singer DAN HILL was born in 1954. His hits included "Sometimes When We Touch" (1977) and "Can't We Try" (1987).
** EVENTS **
1098 : After a five-month siege in the First Crusade, the
Crusaders took Antioch.
1769 : Captain JAMES COOK, a year into his
circumnavigation of the world, observed the transit of Venus over the Sun's disc, the main purpose of his voyage.
1818 : The last of the Maratha Wars between the British
and the Maratha Confederacy in India ended, securing British supremacy in India.
1864 : More than 6,000 Union troops were killed or
wounded in less than an hour at Cold Harbour, during the American Civil War.
1875 : French composer GEORGES BIZET, best-known for his
opera "Carmen", died.
1899 : JOHANN STRAUSS (the younger), who composed "The
Blue Danube", died.
1924 : Austrian novelist FRANZ KAFKA died. He wrote "The
Trial" and "Metamorphosis" and exerted a huge influence on modern writers.
1937 : The former King of England, EDWARD VIII married

WALLIS WARFIELD SIMPSON in Paris, after renouncing the throne. The couple would be known as the DUKE and DUCHESS OF WINDSOR, with only the DUKE to bear the title. EDWARD VIII was a fashionable man, setting many trends including the wearing of tweed sports jackets, cuffed trousers and the 'Windsor' knotted tie. He once said: "Of course I have a slight advantage over the
rest of you. It helps in a pinch to be able to remind your bride that you gave up a throne for her!"
1940 : In World War Two, the evacuation of allied troops
from Dunkirk was completed; over 335,000 British, French and Belgian troops were rescued.
1942 : The United States and Japan began fighting the
Battle of Midway, a new kind of warfare involving air strikes flown from aircraft carriers around the Midway Islands, west-north-west of Hawaii.
1946 : The first bikini bathing suit went on show in
Paris.
1964 : The Rolling Stones began their first tour of the
United States.
1965 : Astronaut EDWARD H. WHITE became the first
American to take a 'walk' in space. Joined to his "Gemini 4" spacecraft by an 'umbilical cord', he drifted for 20 minutes in space.
1969 : The ill-fated Australian aircraft carrier HMAS

MELBOURNE collided with the American destroyer USS FRANK. E. EVANS, cutting the vessel in half and sending it to the bottom of the South China Sea. 74 American sailors died. The disaster was the second involving the Australian ship. On the 10th of February, 1964, MELBOURNE ripped apart the destroyer HMAS VOYAGER, resulting in the deaths of 82 sailors on the smaller vessel.
1973 : A Russian Tupolev-144 supersonic airliner exploded
in mid-air during a demonstration at the Paris Air Show, killing its 6 crew and 9 other people on the ground. Pilot error was blamed for the accident.
1979 : The world's worst oil spillage occurred as a
result of a marine blow-out beneath the drilling rig Ixtoc 1 in the Gulf of Mexico.
1984 : The British Government finally admitted there was
a higher than usual incidence of leukaemia around the controversial Sellafield nuclear station.
1987 : LINDY and MICHAEL CHAMBERLAIN were pardoned by the

Northern Territory Government, over the disappearance of their baby daughter AZARIA at Ayres Rock on the night of Sunday, August 17th, 1980. The couple had maintained their innocence through two inquests, a seven-week trial, two High Court appeals and a Royal Commission. MRS CHAMBERLAIN was jailed for life on the 29th of October, 1982, and freed from prison after serving
three-years and three-months on the 7th of February 1986. Their convictions were quashed on the 15th of September, 1988.
1989 : Ayatollah RUHOLLAH KHOMEINI, spiritual leader of
Iran, died aged 86.
1995 : Defence ministers from NATO and European Union
countries agreed to set up a "rapid reaction force" to protect embattled U.N. peacekeeping troops from Bosnian Serb aggression.
1996 : NATO foreign ministers backed a path-breaking deal
that boosted the role of European members within the Atlantic alliance.
